text: AIPA-47 creates a legal framework for a resilient and prosperous ASEAN

The first plenary session of AIPA-47 took place in Manila (the Philippines) on November 18, chaired by Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines and AIPA-47 President Faustino "Bojie" G. Dy III, according to the Vietnam News Agency.
The session drew parliamentary delegates from AIPA member states, observer parliaments, guests, and AIPA development partners.
The session opened with the admission of the National Parliament of Timor-Leste as an official member of AIPA.

AIPA-47 President Faustino "Bojie" G. Dy III emphasized that expanding to 11 members alongside ASEAN marks a significant milestone, opening a new chapter in AIPA's history with the voices of all Southeast Asian nations represented.
He affirmed that AIPA and member parliaments stand ready to support Timor-Leste in participating fully and effectively in AIPA activities.

Ms. Maria Fernanda Lay, President of the National Parliament of Timor-Leste, expressed her appreciation and affirmed that the admission represents a historic milestone for Timor-Leste after 13 years as an AIPA observer and 24 years of nation-building.
She thanked member parliaments for their support and pledged to actively contribute to the unity and development of AIPA and ASEAN.

During the plenary discussions, heads of parliamentary delegations expressed strong support for the AIPA-47 theme, underscoring the priority of building a peaceful, prosperous, and people-centered ASEAN.
They highlighted AIPA's role in advancing the ASEAN Community Vision 2045, noting that amid rapid global shifts, ASEAN remains a bright spot for stability and growth.

Delegates agreed that ASEAN should continue fostering a culture of dialogue, consultation, and consensus, strengthening strategic trust, upholding international law and the foundational principles of the ASEAN Charter, and promoting cooperation for the practical benefit of citizens.

This includes maintaining peace, stability, and freedom of navigation and overflight, resolving disputes peacefully in accordance with international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and concluding an effective and substantive Code of Conduct (COC) in the East Sea (internationally known as the South China Sea) at an early date.
Parliaments will also work alongside member governments to effectively implement regional commitments and AIPA resolutions.

In his address at the plenary session, Vietnamese National Assembly Chairman Tran Thanh Man praised the AIPA-47 theme and emphasized legislative collaboration in realizing the ASEAN Community Vision 2045.

He stressed that people must always remain at the center, serving as both the goal and the highest driving force of all policies and development decisions across each country and the broader ASEAN Community.

Chairman Man also shared with AIPA members the operational orientation of Vietnam's 16th National Assembly, guided by a proactive, innovative, and development-oriented spirit focused on strengthening institutional foundations and creating breakthroughs for a new development phase of Vietnam toward becoming a developed, high-income country by 2045.
He proposed that AIPA leverage parliamentary diplomacy across three key priorities.

First, strengthening the foundations of peace, stability, and the rule of law by promoting dialogue, building trust, reinforcing ASEAN centrality, and persistently resolving disputes peacefully based on international law, the UN Charter, and the 1982 UNCLOS, while working toward an effective and substantive COC.
Second, establishing a legal framework for a resilient and prosperous ASEAN.

Parliaments should take the lead in institutional reform and legal harmonization to remove trade barriers, boost intra-regional economic integration, and connect supply chains, while prioritizing legal frameworks for emerging growth drivers such as the green economy, digital economy, artificial intelligence governance, just energy transition, and food security so that no country is left behind.

Third, placing people at the center of all parliamentary decisions by strengthening oversight of ASEAN commitment implementation so that citizens and businesses tangibly benefit from integration, and by further promoting the participation of women and youth in political life, policymaking, and mastering future technologies.
Congratulating the National Parliament of Timor-Leste on officially joining the AIPA family, Chairman Man affirmed that Vietnam consistently prioritizes ASEAN in its foreign policy.

He emphasized that as an active and responsible AIPA member, the Vietnamese National Assembly is ready to work closely with member and observer parliaments to build an inclusive, sustainable, and resilient ASEAN Community that truly places people at its center.
